items.title: GDP.xlsx: Benchmarking Frontier Models on Professional Workbooks
items.summary: GDP_xlsx is a benchmark of 70 professional workplace spreadsheet requests across 13 domains, scored with expert rubrics and an agentic judge that opens the workbook.
items.why: It gives teams a rubric-based way to compare frontier models and agents on realistic spreadsheet tasks.

items.title: Activation Steering the Nan-Shan in Typhoon
items.summary: Typhoon is an audiovisual art installation that prompts an LLM seeded with Joseph Conrad's novella to reflect on the current AI moment, using activation steering.

items.title: LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent
items.summary: LuthorSQL is a non-autoregressive 7B text-to-SQL model proposed as a fast first-pass system that could run on local hardware ahead of a slower LLM agent.
items.why: Offloading routine queries to local models could cut API costs and keep sensitive organizational queries off external APIs.

items.title: Towards Seconds-level Video Representation: Quadratically Gated Feature Grid with Adaptive, Prediction-free Sampling
items.summary: Q-GAS is a coordinate-queryable implicit video representation using 3D feature grids, a quadratic-gating decoder, and a prediction-free sampler to speed up building video representations.
items.why: Faster construction of implicit video representations could make them practical for industrial video applications.

items.title: Can Large Language Models Optimize Pretrained Neural Network Weights? A Multi-Phase Empirical Evaluation of Gradient-Free Editing in YOLO26 Object Detection
items.summary: A multi-phase study evaluates whether LLMs can optimize pretrained YOLO26 detector weights gradient-free, comparing them against evolutionary methods and a random-policy control on COCO.
items.why: Results indicate whether LLM guidance adds value over standard search for weight editing of detectors, a question teams weighing that approach need answered.

items.title: Multimodal Person Concept Model for Person Identification under Varying Observation Conditions
items.summary: A multimodal person concept model is proposed that learns person identities from few observations without person labels, for robust identification by service robots under varying conditions.

items.title: CarryOn: Learning What to Keep in Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.summary: CarryOn is a lightweight method that learns which parts of an agent's interaction history to keep in context for long-horizon LLM agent tasks.
items.why: Better context selection addresses the tradeoff between summaries that drop needed details and full histories that add noise in long agent runs.

items.title: SceneAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Portable Game Scene Generation
items.summary: SceneAgent is a multi-agent framework that reuses scene-generation construction processes and experience across different game engine backends via a canonical scene context and backend adapters.
items.why: Separating world state from engine-specific adapters could reduce rework when moving generation pipelines between game engines.

items.title: V-JEPA-LM: Video-Language Models That Read Dynamics Beyond Static, Text-Aligned Representations
items.summary: V-JEPA-LM is a video-language model approach aimed at letting language models use the dynamics captured by V-JEPA video encoders rather than only retrieving static, caption-aligned attributes.
items.why: It highlights that video-LM training can leave useful encoder dynamics unused, relevant to teams building video question-answering systems.

items.title: Tracing Uncertainties of Extreme El Ni\~{n}o Prediction to Mesoscale Ocean Currents
items.summary: Researchers argue that errors in El Niño forecasts may originate from mesoscale errors in initial ocean-current states common to current models and observation systems.
items.why: It shows that small-scale initial-condition errors in ocean data can propagate into large-scale climate forecast uncertainty, relevant to anyone building or validating forecasting pipelines.

items.title: Active Learning of Temporal Specifications through Distinguishing Queries
items.summary: Researchers present an active-learning framework for LTLf that learns temporal logic specifications through learner-teacher interaction, aiming to avoid equivalence queries and restarted SAT searches.
items.why: Automatically learning temporal specifications could reduce the effort of writing verification and monitoring formulas, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: UltraBERT-JEV: Encoder models for System One Applications
items.summary: A technical report compares fine-tuning recipes for UltraBERT-380M encoder models that select among options in one forward pass, reporting 69.7% to 72.1% test accuracy versus 67.6% for Qwen3-0.6B.
items.why: Smaller encoder models may match a much smaller LLM on option-selection tasks at lower inference cost, which matters for cost-sensitive deployments.

items.title: DySENSE: Dynamic Spatiotemporal ENergy Synthesis and Emulation with Satellite Imagery
items.summary: DySENSE is a framework for generating dynamic, spatiotemporal urban energy data and emulating energy use using satellite imagery, aimed at future cities.

items.title: From Local Prediction Error to Final Outputs: A Theory of Expert Sharing in Multi-Step Reasoning
items.summary: A theoretical paper derives criteria for when sharing mixture-of-experts experts across layers or steps reduces local error and still helps final multi-step outputs.
items.why: It gives principled guidance on when expert sharing in MoE architectures improves end-to-end results rather than only local prediction error.

items.title: Photogrammetric 3D Model-Based Animal Behavior Classification
items.summary: Researchers propose classifying animal behavior by first reconstructing 3D body and object geometry from video, then classifying, demonstrated on simulated and real mouse video.

items.title: Securing Multi-Agent Systems by Design
items.summary: Researchers propose response manipulation attacks (ReMA) on multi-agent systems, where malicious agents optimize responses to skew the aggregated final solution, and study securing such systems by design.
items.why: Multi-agent systems that aggregate subagent outputs can be manipulated by a few malicious agents, so aggregation rules and agent trust need security design.

items.title: More Genes, Faster Inference: Efficient Large-Panel Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction from Histology
items.summary: GeneFlow is a framework for predicting expression of large gene panels from histology images, presented as a simpler and more efficient alternative to complex existing methods.

items.title: Condensing Law of Security Information
items.summary: The paper argues that the scaling-law assumption that larger LLMs always do better fails in security, because anomalous, long-tailed inputs such as zero-day attacks are poorly served by likelihood fitting.
items.why: Engineers choosing models for security tasks should not assume bigger models will detect rare anomalies better.

items.title: MineralExp: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Experimental Design in Real-World Mineral Exploration
items.summary: MineralExp is a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on automated geochemical experimental design for real-world mineral exploration.

items.title: Can You Trust Your Finance Agent? Drift, Diagnosis and Auditable Intervention on One Shipped Financial Research Agent
items.summary: The paper audits the reference agent shipped with the Vals Finance Agent Benchmark v2, finding run-to-run score variation and classifying failures by which layer's owner would fix them.
items.why: Shows that leaderboard scores hide instability and cost variation in agents, and that failures need ownership-based diagnosis before deployment.

items.title: From Images to Grounded Edits: A Real-World Benchmark for Chinese Grammatical Error Correction in Handwritten Essays
items.summary: Researchers introduce G-CGEC, a task and benchmark for correcting grammatical errors in handwritten Chinese essay images by predicting both corrections and their positions.
items.why: Image-grounded correction for handwritten K-12 essays extends grammar-correction systems beyond digital text, a gap for education products.

items.title: RL$^{\mathrm{RT}}$: On-Device Reinforcement Learning Runtime
items.summary: RL^RT is an on-device reinforcement learning runtime that shares one embedded GPU between an actor and learner, using a tunable refresh bound and GPU permits, evaluated on Jetson boards.
items.why: Engineers running RL on edge hardware face a tradeoff between actor stalls and policy drift, and this runtime makes that coupling tunable.

items.title: TelePhysica: Agentic Reconstruction of Physically Interactive Scenes
items.summary: TelePhysica is a closed-loop framework that reconstructs physically interactive 3D scenes from a single photograph, aiming for stable, simulatable scenes that support interventions.

items.title: AG-JEPA: Anatomically Guided Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture for Neurodegenerative Representation Learning
items.summary: AG-JEPA adds anatomical tokens to a joint embedding predictive architecture to learn brain MRI representations for detecting early Alzheimer's-related changes.

items.title: EcoVGGT: Pinned-Key Inference for Efficient and Streamable Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction from Long Videos
items.summary: EcoVGGT proposes pinned-key inference, choosing a few dozen evenly spread frames as attention keys for feed-forward 3D reconstruction from long videos, tested on VGGT and π³.
items.why: It targets the quadratic cost of cross-frame attention in multi-view transformers, suggesting a cheaper, streamable path for long-video 3D reconstruction.

items.title: An In-Silico Audit of Topographic Organization in a Multimodal Brain-Response Model
items.summary: An in-silico audit tests whether the TRIBE v2 brain-response model reproduces classic topographic organization such as retinotopy, tonotopy, and MT+ motion selectivity.

items.title: Interpretable weight-space programming builds transparent transformers and brain encoding models
items.summary: Researchers introduce interpretable weight-space programming (iWSP), where an LLM agent builds transparent models by writing their weights and features in code, applied to transformers and brain encoding models.
items.why: It offers a route to interpretable models built by LLM agents, relevant to teams needing explainable predictive systems.

items.title: PUMA-Former: Uncertainty-Aware Agentic Computation Offloading in MEO-LEO Satellite Networks With Incomplete Information
items.summary: PUMA-Former is proposed as an uncertainty-aware agentic framework for cooperative computation offloading across MEO-LEO satellite networks with incomplete CPU state information.

items.title: Who Should Be on the Panel? Task-Conditioned Persona Selection for LLM Trading Agents
items.summary: The paper studies task-conditioned persona selection, composing LLM trading agent panels based on task characteristics, and instantiates it as FinPanel.
items.why: It suggests multi-agent LLM systems should select roles per task rather than reuse a fixed cast, a design choice relevant to agent architects.

items.title: T2ST: Data-Efficient Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models via Temporal Data and Knowledge Transfer
items.summary: T2ST is a data-efficient training framework that augments scarce spatio-temporal data with abundant time-series data to build spatio-temporal foundation models.
items.why: It offers a way to train spatio-temporal foundation models when synchronized observations and spatial metadata are scarce.

items.title: From Pen-and-Paper to Machine-Checked Proofs: Lean for System Identification
items.summary: An introductory paper presents the Lean 4 proof assistant for system identification and control audiences, showing how machine-checked proofs can verify scientific derivations.

items.title: Personalization of Basic and Moral Values Guiding LLM-Controlled Assistant Robots
items.summary: The paper examines how personal LLM-powered assistant robots could be personalized to individual users' basic and moral value profiles rather than an aggregate human value set.
items.why: Shows that per-user value alignment for assistant robots may differ from single aggregate alignment targets, relevant to product design.

items.title: RACE: Ranking-Uncertainty Aware Capacity-Adaptive Customization for Efficient Sequential Recommendation
items.summary: RACE proposes ranking-uncertainty aware, capacity-adaptive model compression for sequential recommendation, varying compression by user intent complexity instead of uniform ratios.
items.why: It offers a way to allocate compute in recommenders by request complexity rather than applying one compression ratio everywhere.

items.title: ParetoM$^3$: Learning on the Pareto Set under Preference Guidance via Min-Max-Min Optimization
items.summary: ParetoM³ proposes a penalty-based min-max-min formulation for preference-guided learning on the weak Pareto set of multiple nonconvex objectives.

items.title: From Bytes to Behavior: Request-Level Attribution from Live GPU Hidden States
items.summary: The paper presents a method to acquire per-layer residual-stream activations from a live GPU LLM process using a non-modifying debugger, enabling request-level attribution.
items.why: It enables forensic analysis of running LLM services that cannot be restarted or modified, useful for incident investigation in production.

items.title: Right Token, Right Time: From Per-Token Gating to Trajectory-Aware Activation Steering
items.summary: The paper proposes trajectory-aware activation steering for LLMs, treating steering with sparse autoencoders as a per-token allocation problem under a fixed budget of steerable tokens.
items.why: It suggests when steering is applied during generation affects output quality, offering a way to control behavior with less degradation.

items.title: PrivacyPR: A Dataset of Real-World Privacy Fixes for Benchmarking Privacy-Aware Code Review
items.summary: PrivacyPR is a dataset of 4,131 merged GitHub pull requests linking real privacy defects and fixes, built to benchmark whether coding agents catch GDPR-relevant issues in code review.
items.why: It provides a benchmark for testing whether AI code review tools catch privacy defects, relevant to compliance-focused engineering teams.

items.title: AI for Parameter Selection in Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization
items.summary: The paper explores whether oracle models can predict quantum runtime and approximation error to select configuration parameters for sample-based quantum diagonalization.

items.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
items.summary: A position piece argues that agentic robotics, where a foundation model runs a closed loop of observing, reasoning, invoking skills, and verifying, is replacing task-specific robot policies.
items.why: It frames a shift from dedicated robot policies to foundation-model agents, though the piece's claims about a specific release are unverified here.

items.title: Vision-Language-Action Models: A Life-Cycle Survey of Design, Training and Deployment
items.summary: A survey reviews 88 vision-language-action (VLA) robot models from December 2022 to October 2026, covering design, training, and deployment across manipulation, navigation, and humanoid control.
items.why: It offers a life-cycle reference for engineers building robot foundation models, from architecture choices through training and deployment.

items.title: AI-Based Multi-View Echocardiographic Image Synthesis using Dynamic Shape Control
items.summary: Researchers propose an AI method for synthesizing multi-view echocardiographic images using dynamic shape control, aiming to reduce reliance on scarce annotated clinical datasets.

items.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
items.summary: Gamer is a generalist vision-language-action agent framework for long-horizon tasks in 2D graphical interfaces and 3D simulated worlds, trained on keyboard and mouse interaction data.
items.why: Unified agents that operate across game and embodied environments show how perception, memory, and multi-step reasoning can be combined in one pipeline.

items.title: CoPre-MoE: Consolidating and Preserving MoE for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
items.summary: CoPre-MoE proposes a mixture-of-experts method for multimodal continual instruction tuning that aims to reduce cross-task redundancy and parameter growth while avoiding catastrophic forgetting.
items.why: Addresses parameter growth in continually updated multimodal models, a practical cost concern for teams fine-tuning MLLMs over time.

items.title: Between Obligations and Evidence: A Participatory Study of Translating the EU AI Act into Technical Requirements
items.summary: A participatory workshop with 32 researchers, policymakers, and practitioners examined how EU AI Act obligations for high-risk systems translate into technical requirements and compliance evidence.
items.why: Shows where interpretation gaps arise when turning EU AI Act obligations into measurable technical compliance evidence.

items.title: Black-Box Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models via Ensemble-of-Ensembles
items.summary: Researchers introduce a black-box two-level ensemble method for LLM uncertainty quantification that aims to separate aleatoric from epistemic uncertainty without white-box access.
items.why: Lets teams using closed LLM APIs distinguish prompt ambiguity from knowledge gaps, improving reliability signals without model internals.

items.title: Do Verifier Judgments Survive Abstraction? Measuring Verification Transport for LLM Agent Evaluation
items.summary: The paper introduces Verification Transport, a test measuring whether LLM verifier judgments of agent executions remain correct when trajectories are abstracted, composed, or compacted.
items.why: Agent evaluators may give different verdicts once tool composition or history compaction hides evidence, affecting how teams trust automated agent checks.

items.title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration
items.summary: A scoping review finds AI-enabled remote patient monitoring is moving toward agentic systems, but most remain human-led and embodied healthcare robotics stays mostly at prototype or pilot stage.
items.why: Indicates that autonomous care agents with real decision-action coupling are still largely experimental, guiding realistic healthcare deployment planning.

items.title: Interactive Program Induction with Language Model Priors
items.summary: The paper studies interactive program induction, using language model priors to resolve ambiguity when recovering a program from a few input-output examples.

items.title: TradeGauntlet: Evaluating Compliance Controls for Autonomous Trading Agents
items.summary: TradeGauntlet is a replayable limit-order-book simulator that evaluates compliance controls for autonomous trading agents, testing 1,680 sessions with Claude Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5.
items.why: Demonstrates how pre-trade gates and reminders trade off detection, prevention, and execution cost for agents operating under compliance constraints.

items.title: Agentic AI for Discovering Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
items.summary: Researchers formulate fault-tolerant quantum circuit design as agentic evolutionary search, aiming to automate circuits for logical state preparation and gates that are now mostly hand-designed.

items.title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading
items.summary: MeReader is a privacy-preserving, offline AI assistant for eBook reading that limits retrieval and generation to the reader's current position to avoid narrative spoilers.
items.why: Illustrates a local-first RAG design that restricts context by reading progress, relevant to privacy-sensitive consumer deployments.

items.title: Elliptic Sampling: Optimal Interpolant Schedules for Gaussians and Beyond
items.summary: The paper introduces a framework for jointly designing interpolant schedules and ODE discretization for generative models based on analyticity, with a conformal-mapping solution for Gaussians.

items.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
items.summary: WeightBench is a benchmark evaluating LLMs on 42 weight-space programming tasks across reading, fixing, and writing neural network weights without gradient descent.
items.why: Provides a standard way to measure whether LLMs can directly read and edit other networks' parameters, an emerging capability.

items.title: From Chats to Markets: AgenticPay for LLM-Powered Negotiation in Multi-Agent Commerce
items.summary: AgenticPay is a benchmark with 160 multimodal tasks across four commerce scenarios and eight market topologies for evaluating LLM agents negotiating multi-issue agreements in competitive markets.
items.why: Gives teams a testbed for assessing how autonomous agents negotiate and transact in multi-agent markets before deploying them commercially.

items.title: Evaluating Chain-of-Thought Reasoning through Reusability and Verifiability
items.summary: Researchers study whether chain-of-thought reasoning passed between a Sender LLM and a Receiver LLM is reliable, useful, and safe.
items.why: Multi-model pipelines pass reasoning traces downstream, so engineers need to know whether that transferred reasoning can be trusted and acted on.

items.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Multimodal Large Language Models with Incoherence-adjusted Semantic Volume
items.summary: Researchers introduce UMPIRE, a training-free uncertainty quantification framework for multimodal LLMs intended to flag unreliable outputs.
items.why: Reliable uncertainty signals could let teams route risky multimodal queries to human experts or larger models without extra training.

items.title: Multi-Environment POMDPs with Finite-Horizon Objectives
items.summary: Researchers study computing optimal values and policies for multi-environment POMDPs with finite-horizon objectives, where the initial state is adversarially chosen.

items.title: Do LLMs Experience an Internal Polylogue? Investigating Reasoning through the Lens of Personas
items.summary: Researchers treat LLM persona vectors as dynamic probes, tracking their alignment with hidden activations during reasoning across four open-weight models.
items.why: Monitoring persona signals during generation could offer a way to observe and steer model behavior mid-reasoning rather than only statically.

items.title: D-VLA: A High-Concurrency Distributed Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning Framework for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Researchers present D-VLA, a distributed asynchronous reinforcement learning framework for training Vision-Language-Action models at high concurrency.
items.why: Addresses throughput bottlenecks from balancing physical simulation against VRAM and bandwidth demands when running RL on large VLA models.

items.title: ShopGym: An Integrated Framework for Realistic Simulation and Scalable Benchmarking of E-Commerce Web Agents
items.summary: Researchers present ShopGym, a framework for simulating and benchmarking e-commerce web agents in reproducible, scalable environments.
items.why: Offers a controllable alternative to live storefronts for evaluating shopping agents, which teams building web agents need for repeatable comparisons.

items.title: Certified Policy Optimisation for Nested Causal Bandits via PAC-Bayes Risk
items.summary: Researchers propose Nested Causal Thompson Sampling for nested contextual causal bandits, where a strategic decision shapes the context for later tactical choices.

items.title: CoffeeBench: Benchmarking Long-Horizon LLM Agents in Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Economies
items.summary: Researchers introduce CoffeeBench, a benchmark where six LLM coding agents run farmers, roasters, and retailers in a simulated coffee supply chain.
items.why: Shows a way to test long-horizon multi-agent business behavior in simulated economies, relevant to assessing agents before deploying them in business roles.

items.title: Hallucination-Free GUI Grounding via Regression-Free Layout-Aware Matching
items.summary: Researchers propose a regression-free, layout-aware matching method to reduce coordinate hallucinations in visual MLLM-based GUI grounding.
items.why: Coordinate hallucinations are a practical reliability problem for screenshot-based GUI agents that must click precise elements.

items.title: ReForge: Keeping ABR Algorithms Never Finished with Verified Large Language Model Revisions
items.summary: Researchers propose ReForge, which revises ABR video streaming algorithms with verified LLM edits after deployment without degrading performance on networks already served.
items.why: Shows a path to continuously improving deployed networking policies with LLMs while guarding against regressions on existing conditions.

items.title: Programmable Distributions of Semantics-Preserving Variants for Evaluating Code Agents
items.summary: Researchers evaluate coding agents on semantically equivalent rewrites of repositories, finding resolve rates can shift under superficial code variations.
items.why: Suggests coding agent benchmarks may overstate reliability, since behavior can change when code is rewritten without altering its meaning.

items.title: From Regulation to Implementation: A Critical Evaluation of LLM-Assisted Regulatory Compliance in Industry
items.summary: A critical evaluation examines using LLMs to help create EU regulatory compliance artifacts such as Digital Product Passports and GDPR impact assessments in industry.
items.why: Gives compliance and engineering leaders evidence on how far LLM-assisted documentation can meet EU requirements in practice.

items.title: AI Agents Push Humans Out of the Loop
items.summary: A position paper argues current AI agent designs undermine effective human oversight and degrade the cognitive capacities oversight requires.
items.why: Challenges the assumption that keeping a human in the loop is sufficient, which affects how teams design agent oversight.

items.title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation through Human-Agent Interaction
items.summary: Researchers propose efficient test-time adaptation via iterative human-agent interaction to capture criteria users cannot fully specify upfront.
items.why: Suggests a way to tailor agent outputs to individual expert standards through repeated interaction rather than upfront specification.

items.title: MeanFlowAdvantage: Stable Reward Fine-Tuning for Few-Step Average-Velocity Generators
items.summary: Researchers introduce MeanFlowAdvantage, a reward fine-tuning objective for few-step average-velocity generators that matches the inference-time average-velocity map.

items.title: Proof-Grounded Patient-Specific Clinical Explanations from Knowledge-Graph Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers describe the CKG Clinical Explanation Engine, which turns knowledge-graph reasoning outputs into typed facts, rule traces, and provenance-linked clinical recommendations.
items.why: It targets auditable clinical decision support, where engineers building healthcare systems need traceable links from observations to recommendations.

items.title: When to Rethink: Learning Multi-Perspective Self-Verification for Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Researchers propose a multi-perspective self-verification method for vision-language models to better detect plausible but incorrect answers without external judges.
items.why: More reliable self-verification could reduce wrong answers from multimodal systems without adding external judge models.

items.title: Self-Building Labs
items.summary: Researchers introduce a self-building laboratory that designs, configures, and operates its own lab setup from a high-level scientific goal.

items.title: TorchTPU - A Hybrid Eager/Compiled Architecture for Native PyTorch Execution on TPU
items.summary: Google and Meta describe TorchTPU, an open-source native PyTorch backend for Google TPUs supporting eager execution and torch.compile integration.
items.why: Engineers running PyTorch can migrate models to TPUs with less rework, using a native backend rather than a separate port.

items.title: FlashRT-PAI: Fast Kernels Are Not Fast Pipelines for Physical AI
items.summary: FlashRT-PAI targets real-time inference latency in physical AI models, arguing system-level overhead, not kernel speed, dominates vision-language-action pipelines.
items.why: Robotics teams optimizing real-time inference may find kernel-level speedups insufficient without addressing pipeline overhead.

items.title: Pluralistic Alignment in Large Language Models: Objectives, Human References, and Preference Representations
items.summary: A survey proposes a two-layer taxonomy for pluralistic alignment in LLMs, separating target behavior, whose preferences define the reference, and evidence of success.

items.title: TimesJev: Thinking Fast on Time Series with System 1 Sufficiency
items.summary: TimesJev proposes using fast System 1 models for time series reasoning, aiming to avoid the thousands of tokens long chain-of-thought reasoning requires.
items.why: Reducing reasoning tokens could cut inference latency for time series applications that currently depend on long chain-of-thought outputs.

items.title: Can LLMs Improve Their Own Harness? A Controlled Study on ARC-AGI-3
items.summary: A controlled study examines whether LLMs can improve their own harness, the scaffold orchestrating model calls, on the ARC-AGI-3 interactive benchmark.
items.why: Self-improving agent scaffolds bear on how much human engineering agent harnesses will require in future.

items.title: One Offset, Two Directions: Baseline Adjustment via Subgroup Offsets
items.summary: Researchers propose subgroup-based baseline adjustment for GRPO, arguing the global within-prompt mean baseline collapses heterogeneous rollout subgroups with distinct rewards.
items.why: Better advantage baselines could improve reinforcement learning fine-tuning of reasoning models that use GRPO.

items.title: Function-Preserving Audits of Visual Weight Readers
items.summary: Researchers show visual readers of neural field weights can be highly accurate on original weights yet sensitive to function-preserving equivalent representations.

items.title: AttentionSwitch: Jailbreak Defense for LLMs via Joint Learning of Sparse Attention-Head Selection and Scaling
items.summary: AttentionSwitch proposes a jailbreak defense for LLMs that jointly learns sparse attention-head selection and scaling, avoiding costly fine-tuning.
items.why: Targeted component interventions offer a potentially cheaper alternative to fine-tuning for hardening LLMs against jailbreaks.

items.title: ABHBench: Evaluating Moral Decision-Making of Foundation Models from an Agentic Perspective
items.summary: ABHBench is a multimodal benchmark built from the game Detroit: Become Human that tests how foundation models make moral decisions as acting agents.
items.why: Evaluating models as first-person agents exposes moral behavior that third-person vignette benchmarks miss, relevant to autonomous deployments.

items.title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
items.summary: Sage-Taiyi is a metacognition-inspired architecture that guides scientific investigation, reporting first place on all eight metrics of the Taiyi-Bench ideation benchmark.

items.title: AutoManifold: Agentic Design of Data Visualisation Algorithms via Manifold Embedding
items.summary: AutoManifold is an agentic pipeline that generates data visualisation embedding algorithms tailored to user-specified structural priorities.
items.why: Shows agents automating algorithm design for user-specified objectives, a pattern applicable to other engineering tooling.

items.title: MIGRO: A Decoupled and Portable Long-Term Memory System for Language Models
items.summary: MIGRO is a decoupled long-term memory system that keeps interaction history as persistent state shared across successive language models.
items.why: A model-independent memory layer could let teams swap underlying LLMs without losing accumulated user context.

items.title: Small Heads, Strong Decisions: A Controlled Study of Typed-Decision Models
items.summary: A controlled study compares typed-decision models, which read text with a language model and output calibrated yes/no, choice, or graded-score decisions.
items.why: Typed decision heads could cut inference cost for routing and classification, but the text gives few concrete results to judge them by.

items.title: Benchmarking AI risk behaviors
items.summary: Researchers present a toolkit that profiles LLM risk propensities, measuring how risk-averse or consistent models are across contexts and generations.
items.why: Standardized risk profiles could help teams predict model behavior and compare model generations before deploying them in sensitive settings.

items.title: S1-Evo: Experience-Guided Evidence Competition Attacks on Typed System-1 Decision Models
items.summary: S1-Evo proposes a self-evolving attack framework that manipulates typed System-1 decision models used for routing, moderation, and authorization in LLM agents.
items.why: Agents relying on typed decision models for authorization may be vulnerable to context-based manipulation, so these attacks matter for defense design.

items.title: Ballad: Bandit-Based LLM Routing for Automated Heuristic Discovery
items.summary: Ballad uses bandit-based routing across LLMs for automated heuristic discovery, finding no consistent advantage for larger, costlier models on NP-hard problems.
items.why: Engineers may be able to cut costs in automated optimization pipelines by routing among cheaper models rather than always using the most expensive one.

items.title: Fake News Detectors are Biased against Texts Generated by Large Language Models
items.summary: A study finds many fake news detectors are biased, more often flagging LLM-generated texts as fake than human-written ones.
items.why: Teams using automated detectors to filter content should check for bias against machine-generated text, since it can skew moderation outcomes.

items.title: Astraios: Parameter-Efficient Instruction Tuning Code Large Language Models
items.summary: Astraios is a suite of 28 instruction-tuned code models comparing seven parameter-efficient tuning methods across four model sizes up to 16 billion parameters.
items.why: The comparison of tuning methods across scales helps engineers pick cost-effective fine-tuning approaches for code models.

items.title: BigCodeBench: Benchmarking Code Generation with Diverse Function Calls and Complex Instructions
items.summary: BigCodeBench is a benchmark testing code generation that uses diverse function calls and complex instructions, beyond short algorithmic tasks.
items.why: It offers a more realistic test of whether code models can use multiple tools for practical tasks, informing model selection.

items.title: Benign Overfitting for Regression with Trained Two-Layer ReLU Networks
items.summary: A theoretical paper proves generalization results for two-layer ReLU networks trained by gradient flow in the neural tangent kernel regime.

items.title: LEGAL-UQA: Testing Constitutional Question-Answering Systems for Urdu Speakers with a Parallel English-Urdu Benchmark
items.summary: LEGAL-UQA is a parallel English-Urdu benchmark of 619 question-answer pairs based on Pakistan's Constitution, for testing constitutional question answering.
items.why: It shows how multilingual legal assistants need language-specific evaluation data, which teams building non-English RAG systems should account for.

items.title: AbFlowNet: Optimizing Antibody-Antigen Binding Energy via Diffusion-GFlowNet Fusion
items.summary: AbFlowNet combines diffusion and GFlowNet methods to jointly optimize antibody CDR design for antigen binding energy.

items.title: Chi-Square Wavelet Graph Neural Networks for Heterogeneous Graph Anomaly Detection
items.summary: ChiGAD is a spectral graph neural network framework for anomaly detection in heterogeneous graphs, addressing meta-path semantics and class imbalance.

items.title: Graph Your Own Prompt
items.summary: Graph Consistency Regularization (GCR) injects relational graph structure derived from model predictions into training to produce more class-aware representations.

items.title: BigCodeArena: Unveiling More Reliable Human Preferences in Code Generation via Execution
items.summary: BigCodeArena is an open human evaluation platform for code generation that runs generated code on the fly so raters can judge execution results.
items.why: Execution-based human preference evaluation may give more reliable model comparisons for coding tasks than reading raw code.

items.title: Manifold Approximation leads to Robust Kernel Alignment
items.summary: Manifold-approximated Kernel Alignment (MKA) modifies centered kernel alignment to account for data manifold geometry, aiming for more robust representation comparisons.

items.title: E0: Expressive Fine-Grained Discrete Action Prediction for Vision-Language-Action Models via Tweedie Discrete Diffusion
items.summary: E0 proposes discrete diffusion for fine-grained action prediction in vision-language-action robotics models to produce more stable, expressive actions.
items.why: Robotics teams building VLA systems may find more stable action outputs useful, though the text gives no benchmark results.

items.title: Model-Free Assessment of Simulator Fidelity via Quantile Curves
items.summary: Researchers propose a model-free method using quantile curves to assess how well simulators match real systems across scenarios, quantifying the sim-to-real gap.
items.why: Gives teams a way to measure simulator fidelity without needing direct observations of the real system's latent parameters.

items.title: NEAT: Neighborhood-Guided, Efficient, Autoregressive Set Transformer for 3D Molecular Generation
items.summary: Researchers introduce NEAT, a neighborhood-guided autoregressive set transformer that generates 3D molecules without relying on canonical atom orderings.
items.why: Offers an efficient transformer alternative to diffusion models for 3D molecule generation that is permutation invariant over atoms.

items.title: Vision-language models lag human performance on physical dynamics and intent reasoning
items.summary: Researchers introduce Teleo-Spatial Intelligence, a benchmark finding vision-language models lag humans at reasoning about physical dynamics and human intent.
items.why: Highlights a gap in VLM spatial and intent reasoning that matters for embodied and real-world human-environment applications.

items.title: ISLA: Ensemble learning and domain adaptation for generalizable acute ischemic stroke lesion segmentation in diffusion MRI with clinical validation
items.summary: Researchers present ISLA, an ensemble nnU-Net-based framework for acute ischemic stroke lesion segmentation in diffusion MRI, aimed at generalizing to unseen clinical sites.
items.why: Addresses poor generalization of medical segmentation models across clinical sites, with external clinical validation.

items.title: Tracing 3D Anatomy in 2D Strokes: Can Projection-Derived Masks Replace 3D Segmentation for Cervical Spine Fracture Recognition?
items.summary: Researchers test whether masks approximated from 2D projections can replace full 3D vertebra segmentation for detecting cervical spine fractures in CT.
items.why: Suggests a potentially cheaper pipeline for CT fracture recognition that avoids full 3D segmentation.

items.title: The Alignment Curse: Modality Alignment Supercharges Audio Attacks via Text Transfer
items.summary: Researchers show that modality alignment in end-to-end omni-models can let text-based jailbreak attacks transfer to audio, potentially underestimating audio-related risks.
items.why: Suggests current audio safety evaluations may miss risks inherited from text, so teams deploying omni-models should test cross-modal attacks.

items.title: ROCKET: Rapid Optimization via Calibration-guided Knapsack Enhanced Truncation for Efficient Model Compression
items.summary: ROCKET is a training-free model compression method that allocates layer-wise compression via a multi-choice knapsack formulation under a global size budget.
items.why: Offers a training-free way to compress models to a target size while minimizing reconstruction error, reducing retraining costs.

items.title: ScrapeGraphAI-100k: Dataset for Schema-Constrained LLM Generation
items.summary: Researchers release ScrapeGraphAI-100k, a dataset of 93,695 schema-constrained extraction events pairing real web page content with JSON schemas and prompts.
items.why: Provides realistic, real-world data for training and evaluating structured JSON output from LLMs.

items.title: ESENSC: A Polynomial-Time Axiomatic Alternative to SHAP
items.summary: Researchers propose ESENSC, a deterministic closed-form feature attribution rule that approximates SHAP values using linearly many coalition evaluations.
items.why: Offers a faster, deterministic alternative to SHAP for explaining tabular model predictions, with close agreement to exact SHAP.

items.title: ViroGym: Realistic Large-Scale Benchmarks for Evaluating Viral Proteins
items.summary: Researchers introduce ViroGym, a large benchmark evaluating protein language models on viral protein variant effect prediction across multiple tasks.
items.why: Provides a systematic benchmark for judging whether protein models are reliable for anticipating viral mutations.

items.title: Efficiently Aligning Draft Models via Parameter- and Data-Efficient Adaptation
items.summary: Researchers propose Efficient Draft Adaptation (EDA), a parameter- and data-efficient framework for adapting speculative decoding draft models to fine-tuned target models.
items.why: Lets teams keep speculative decoding speedups after domain fine-tuning without costly full draft model retraining.

items.title: A Variational Latent Equilibrium for Learning in Neuronal Circuits
items.summary: Researchers propose a biologically plausible formalism that approximates backpropagation through time in neuronal circuits using a variational latent equilibrium approach.
items.why: Foundational neuroscience-inspired learning research with limited direct near-term applicability for engineering teams.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of 3D Convolutional and 2.5D Slice-Conditioned U-Net Architectures for MRI Super-Resolution via Elucidated Diffusion Models
items.summary: Researchers compare 3D convolutional and 2.5D slice-conditioned U-Net backbones for 2x brain MRI super-resolution using elucidated diffusion models.
items.why: Compares architecture tradeoffs for diffusion-based MRI enhancement, a software alternative to higher-field scanners.

items.title: FlashSampling: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Sampling
items.summary: Researchers present FlashSampling, an exact sampling primitive that fuses categorical sampling into the LM-head matmul without materializing the logits tensor in HBM.
items.why: Reduces memory traffic and kernel launches in large-vocabulary LLM decoding, directly relevant to inference performance work.

items.title: Generative machine learning for protein design
items.summary: A review of 59 generative AI approaches across six protein design tasks, covering sequence, backbone, and structure-conditioned generation.
items.why: Gives a consolidated map of generative protein design methods for teams evaluating tools for therapeutics or enzyme engineering.

items.title: Pruning Extensions and Efficiency Trade-Offs for Sustainable Time Series Classification
items.summary: Researchers propose a multi-dimensional framework for benchmarking resource-versus-quality trade-offs in time series classification, plus a bounded-error pruning strategy for Hydra and Quant.
items.why: Offers practical methods to cut compute for time series classifiers at scale, which matters when serving costs and energy budgets are constraints.

items.title: Minimizing classical resources in variational measurement-based quantum computation for generative modeling
items.summary: Researchers study minimizing classical processing in variational measurement-based quantum computation for generative modeling.

items.title: Generating Concept Lexicalizations via Dictionary-Based Cross-Lingual Sense Projection
items.summary: Researchers present a method that expands WordNet-style lexical resources to new languages by projecting senses across aligned corpora using a bilingual dictionary.
items.why: Relevant mainly to teams building multilingual NLP resources, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: CPGRec+: A Balance-oriented Framework for Personalized Video Game Recommendations
items.summary: Researchers extend CPGRec into CPGRec+, a graph-based video game recommender that balances accuracy and diversity while weighting player-game interactions differently.

items.title: Screen Before You Interpret: A Portable Validity Screen for Benchmark-Based LLM Confidence Signals
items.summary: Researchers propose a portable validity screen that checks whether LLM confidence signals actually vary with correctness before metrics are computed on them.
items.why: Teams using LLM confidence for abstention or escalation can use this check to avoid acting on signals that don't track correctness.

items.title: BoostLoRA: Growing Effective Rank by Boosting Adapters
items.summary: Researchers introduce BoostLoRA, a gradient-boosting approach that iteratively trains and merges minimal adapters on mispredicted examples to grow effective rank in parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
items.why: Suggests a way to raise expressivity of ultra-low-parameter fine-tuning adapters without increasing adapter size per round.

items.title: Time series causal discovery with variable lags
items.summary: Researchers present a method for learning causal structure from time-series data where dependencies occur at variable time lags.

items.title: Exposing and Mitigating Temporal Attack in Deepfake Video Detection
items.summary: Researchers show spatiotemporal deepfake detectors overfit to fragile temporal spectrum cues and propose SpInShield, a spectral-invariant defense against evasion attacks.
items.why: Highlights that high-AUC deepfake detectors can be easily evaded, relevant to teams deploying detection in adversarial settings.

items.title: Hybrid Mechanical and Agentic Specification Inference
items.summary: Researchers describe a hybrid of mechanical and LLM-agent specification inference for Move smart contracts, integrated into the Move Prover verifier.
items.why: Shows an agentic LLM loop driving formal verification tooling, which may reduce the manual cost of writing contracts for smart contract teams.

items.title: Wavelet Flow Matching for Multi-Scale Physics Emulation
items.summary: Researchers propose Wavelet Flow Matching, a generative emulator for multi-scale PDE physics that aims to avoid the cost of separately pre-trained autoencoders.

items.title: TransitLM: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Map-Free Transit Route Generation
items.summary: Researchers release TransitLM, a dataset of about 13 million transit route records from four Chinese cities for training LLMs to generate routes without map infrastructure.
items.why: Provides a large benchmark and continual pre-training corpus for LLM-based route generation, though the text gives limited evaluation detail.

items.title: DeltaBox: Millisecond-Scale Sandbox Checkpoint and Rollback for Stateful AI Agents
items.summary: Researchers introduce DeltaBox, a sandbox checkpoint and rollback system that stores only state differences to reach millisecond-scale restores for stateful AI agents.
items.why: Faster sandbox checkpoint and restore could remove a bottleneck for agent tree search and RL workloads that need many state branches.

items.title: Larch: Learned Query Optimization for Semantic Predicates
items.summary: Researchers present Larch, a learned query optimizer for semantic predicates in AI SQL queries that call costly LLM-based semantic operators.
items.why: Addresses high inference cost of semantic operators in database queries, which matters to teams running LLM-powered analytics at scale.

items.title: QVal: Evaluating Dense Supervision Signals for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.summary: Researchers introduce QVal, a training-free testbed that measures how well dense supervision signals order intermediate steps for long-horizon LLM agents.
items.why: Offers a cheaper way to compare dense reward signals for agent training without running full training pipelines.

items.title: When Simpler Is Better: Evaluating Translation Pipelines for Medieval Latin Manuscripts
items.summary: Researchers evaluate image-to-translation pipelines for medieval Latin manuscripts, finding that simpler approaches can outperform more complex ones on vision-language tasks.
items.why: Shows vision-language models struggle on noisy historical documents, a caution for OCR and translation pipelines in low-resource domains.

items.title: URSA: Chemistry-Aware Benchmark for Utilitarian Retrosynthesis Assessment
items.summary: Researchers introduced URSA, a chemistry-aware benchmark framework for evaluating retrosynthesis planning systems, including deep-learning tools and general-purpose LLMs.
items.why: It offers a chemically interpretable way to compare retrosynthesis systems, which helps teams choose tools for drug discovery workflows.

items.title: Input Pathways Shape Few-Shot, Not Zero-Shot, Binding in Tiny Transformers: A Fully-Enumerable Study
items.summary: A study of ~6-10K-parameter transformers on exhaustively enumerated factored worlds finds input encoding affects few-shot but not zero-shot compositional binding.

items.title: REFORGE: A Method for Benchmarking LLMs' Reverse Engineering Capabilities in Decompiled Binary Function Naming
items.summary: Researchers propose REFORGE, a method for benchmarking LLMs on naming decompiled binary functions, arguing existing benchmarks skip reliable ground-truth construction.
items.why: Current LLM reverse-engineering accuracy claims may overstate capability because evaluable function counts are rarely disclosed, affecting security tool assessments.

items.title: CPM-MultiAgent: A CPM-Grounded Appraisal Framework for Simulating Dynamic Patient Emotional Evolution in Healthcare Dialogue
items.summary: CPM-MultiAgent is a framework for simulating how a virtual patient's emotions evolve across healthcare dialogue, aimed at communication training.

items.title: Courteous Anticipation: Improving Long-Lived Task Planning in Persistent Shared Environments
items.summary: Researchers propose a planning approach where robots sharing a persistent environment anticipate how their actions affect future tasks for all robots.
items.why: Multi-robot planners that ignore downstream effects can accumulate costs over long task sequences, relevant to fleet and warehouse automation.

items.title: When Does On-Policy Interaction Help? Representational Tradeoffs in Value-Based Imitation Learning
items.summary: A paper examines when on-policy expert querying helps value-based imitation learning, analyzing representational tradeoffs versus behavior cloning.

items.title: Cloud-Edge LLM Collaborative Learning via Accelerating Personalized Bilevel Optimization
items.summary: Researchers propose a personalized bilevel optimization framework for cloud-edge LLM collaboration, balancing global consensus with local edge personalization.
items.why: Cloud-edge LLM deployments must balance shared knowledge with per-device adaptation, a practical architecture question for teams deploying models at the edge.

items.title: Hidden not Deleted: How Networks Suppress Entangled Features
items.summary: A small autoencoder study shows that suppressed neural network features are often hidden behind activation thresholds rather than deleted.

items.title: From Data to Program: Fast & Direct Generative Program Inference from Empirical Data
items.summary: PRODiGI is a pretrained model that infers an executable generative program from data samples in a single forward pass.
items.why: Direct data-to-program inference could replace dataset-specific density model fitting, though the text gives limited detail on practical performance.

items.title: Parameterization method of reservoir properties for ensemble-based data assimilation using intermediate latent space of StyleGAN
items.summary: Researchers propose parameterizing reservoir properties using StyleGAN's intermediate latent space for ensemble-based history matching of non-Gaussian geology.

items.title: Cross-Benchmark Transfer from RL on Agentic Coding Tasks
items.summary: Researchers post-trained Kimi K2.7 Code, a 1T-parameter open-weight MoE model, using RL on 1,700 expert-built agentic coding tasks to study transfer across benchmarks.
items.why: RL on agentic coding tasks may close the 'last mile' gaps in coding agents, relevant to teams building or evaluating coding assistants.

items.title: Nearly Optimal Fixed-Confidence Best-Arm Identification with 1-Bit Feedback
items.summary: A paper studies fixed-confidence best-arm identification under strict 1-bit feedback, developing a time-uniform 1-bit mean-estimation primitive.

items.title: What Should World Models Forget? Stratified Retention for Continual Adaptation
items.summary: Researchers argue that world models should selectively retain knowledge, treating accurate-then-outdated information as correct revision rather than forgetting.
items.why: Continual-learning evaluation that counts necessary revisions as forgetting may misjudge world model quality in changing environments.

items.title: Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction
items.summary: Researchers train a small MLP head to locate where to intervene in failed LLM reasoning rollouts, finding inline injections often fail to redirect reasoning.
items.why: Shows that naive inline correction prompts may not reliably fix LLM reasoning errors under fixed generation budgets.

items.title: Learning to Read Out: Unembedding Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining
items.summary: A paper introduces parameter-trajectory tracking to measure when a language model's unembedding readout expresses capabilities its hidden states already encode.
items.why: Output-based capability timelines may misdate when models acquire skills, which matters for evaluating training progress and checkpoints.

items.title: Brain2Vec: A Self-Supervised 3D Foundation Model for Structural Brain MRI
items.summary: Researchers introduced Brain2Vec, a self-supervised 3D foundation model pre-trained on 74,425 T1-weighted brain MRI scans, usable for fine-tuning or as a feature extractor.
items.why: Shows pretraining a large medical imaging foundation model on pooled data can serve as a reusable backbone when labeled data is scarce.

items.title: Operationalizing Governed Agentic Workflows in Regulated Finance: A Customer Zero Case Study using Zafin AIOS
items.summary: Researchers presented Zafin AIOS, an orchestration platform and control plane for deploying governed AI-assisted development in regulated finance, with a case study comparing AI-assisted and human-led work.
items.why: Offers architectural patterns for governance controls that teams in regulated industries need to move AI development from pilots to production.

items.title: EmbodiExp: Compositional Experience Transfer for Embodied Agents
items.summary: Researchers propose EmbodiExp, a framework that builds outcome-verified subgoal experiences for embodied agents and composes them to transfer experience across tasks with shared subgoals.
items.why: Suggests reusable, verified subgoal experiences may help robotic agents generalize across tasks, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: NaijaFacts: A Framework for Disentangling Language from Knowledge in Facts about Nigeria
items.summary: Researchers released NaijaFacts, a benchmark of native-speaker-authored factual questions about Nigeria in English, Nigerian Pidgin, Yoruba, Igbo and Hausa, compared against UK and US questions.
items.why: Separates factual knowledge from language competence in multilingual evaluation, which matters for teams assessing models on African-language content.

items.title: Accepted but Wrong: Silent Failures of LLM Code Repairs after API Migrations
items.summary: A preregistered study of 73 tasks across 60 API changes in CPython, Node.js and SQLite found LLM code repairs can run cleanly yet return wrong results that typical-input checks miss.
items.why: Shows typical-input release checks let many wrong LLM-generated repairs ship, so teams need edge-case tests derived from release notes.

items.title: All Quiet on the Neural Front: Language Models Do Not Report Injected Pain States
items.summary: A study found that three open-weight language models cannot report when an injected pain direction is active, across every protocol tested using the OWMI method.
items.why: Indicates that models' self-reports about internal states are unreliable, which matters for anyone relying on model introspection for safety monitoring.

items.title: Agentic-OPD: Recovering Forgotten Agent Capabilities via On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Tasks
items.summary: Agentic-OPD proposes recovering capabilities from discarded RL checkpoints by using earlier checkpoints as a teacher pool for on-policy distillation in agentic LLM training.
items.why: Suggests checkpoints normally discarded during GRPO agent training can be reused at no extra training cost to recover solved problems.

items.title: Before Words, Beyond Speech: Evaluating Nonverbal Social Reasoning in Early Childhood
items.summary: Researchers introduced NESTI, a benchmark for evaluating nonverbal social reasoning in early-childhood videos, focusing on gaze, gesture and physical contact.
items.why: Highlights a gap in multimodal video benchmarks, which mostly target adult conversational interaction.

items.title: Deletion Sensitivity Is a Property of the Model: A Three-Condition Measurement over 72 Valid Experimental Cells
items.summary: A multi-seed study across 72 valid experimental cells measured how deleting full reasoning history in multi-turn tool-calling sessions affects model task performance.
items.why: Shows deleting history when requests cross providers can change task outcomes, relevant for teams routing multi-turn agent traffic across issuers.

items.title: Stochastic Projections and Rank-Aware Learning Rates for Federated LoRA
items.summary: Researchers propose stochastic projections and rank-aware learning rates for federated LoRA fine-tuning, arguing frozen-A LoRA with Gaussian initialization approximates full fine-tuning.
items.why: Offers theory and methods for communication-efficient fine-tuning of foundation models across resource-constrained distributed clients.

items.title: ForeSpark: Joint Draft and Verification Budget Scheduling for Parallel Speculative Decoding
items.summary: ForeSpark proposes jointly scheduling draft and verification budgets for parallel speculative decoding, noting drafting can consume up to 40% of step time at high serving load.
items.why: Targets wasted compute in LLM serving, where most drafted tokens are discarded, which directly affects inference throughput and cost.

items.title: TransGHOST: Real-Time, Synthesis-Free Reconstruction of Instrument-Occluded Regions in Ophthalmic Microsurgery
items.summary: Researchers present TransGHOST, a causal, reference-guided method for real-time reconstruction of tissue occluded by instruments in ophthalmic microsurgery video, without synthesis.
items.why: Relevant to robot-assisted surgical systems that need reliable scene perception, though the text offers little on deployment readiness.

items.title: CastWorld: Benchmarking Context-Aware Agentic Time Series Forecasting Beyond Predictive Accuracy
items.summary: Researchers introduced CastWorld, an agentic benchmark for context-aware time series forecasting spanning 8 domains and 25 real-world datasets.
items.why: Provides a way to evaluate forecasting agents beyond numerical accuracy, including their use of contextual information.

items.title: CARE-Drive: Coupled Alternating Refinement for Ego-trajectories
items.summary: CARE-Drive proposes coupled alternating refinement of ego-trajectories for vision-language-action models in end-to-end autonomous driving, specializing refinement across physical quantities.
items.why: Offers a trajectory refinement approach for VLA-based driving models, though the text gives little on measured gains.

items.title: JudgeMix: Judge-Guided Mixed-Rollout Data Synthesis for LLM Agents
items.summary: JudgeMix proposes judge-guided mixed-rollout data synthesis to train LLM agents, aiming to ground supervised fine-tuning data in the target model's own state distribution.
items.why: Addresses the training-inference distribution mismatch in agent SFT, a practical issue for teams fine-tuning agents on expert trajectories.

items.title: Indic-Task Gains and Regressions after Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Researchers applied GRPO reinforcement learning to a 30B-A3B mixture-of-experts model covering English and eight Indic languages, finding math gains alongside Indic QA regressions.
items.why: RL post-training can lift some benchmarks while silently degrading others, such as low-resource language QA, so multilingual evals need checking before and after tuning.

items.title: Rectified Looped Transformer
items.summary: Researchers propose Rectified Looped Transformer, which redesigns loop feedback with an interpolation schedule to avoid hidden-state scale growth in looped language models.
items.why: Looped transformers offer parameter-efficient depth, and this addresses instability that grows as recurrence deepens, relevant to efficient model architecture choices.

items.title: HyBridge: Bridge-Guided Self-Supervised Hyperbolic Hypergraph Representation Learning
items.summary: Researchers present HyBridge, a self-supervised hyperbolic hypergraph representation learning method that uses bridge-node structure to guide embeddings.

items.title: ZONOS3-Mini Technical Report
items.summary: Zyphra released a technical report for ZONOS3-Mini, an 886M-parameter zero-shot voice-cloning TTS model with a new audio codec, claiming real-time performance on laptops and phones.
items.why: A compact, on-device voice-cloning model with a new codec could enable low-latency speech features without cloud inference costs.

items.title: Tracing Knowledge and Reasoning in LLM
items.summary: Researchers propose a task-centric framework that combines attention, activation, and representation signals to characterize model-internal processing elicited by LLM benchmarks.
items.why: Going beyond aggregate benchmark scores to inspect internal processing can reveal failure modes that task-level metrics hide when comparing models.

items.title: Poetry 'resurrection' from LLMs
items.summary: Researchers tested whether AI can write an infinite poem using couplets with poetic end-word relationships, finding AI produces interesting pairings but falls short of human creativity.

items.title: Creating Steering Vectors via Input Optimisation
items.summary: Researchers introduce ActGCG, which optimizes a text suffix to mimic activation steering effects, plus universal suffixes and a step that rewrites suffixes into readable text.
items.why: It suggests steering-like behavior could be induced through prompts alone, without white-box access to hidden states, which matters for deployed model control.

items.title: CamSpokenNLI: A Pilot Resource for Cross-Variety Transfer Evaluation in Cameroon Pidgin English and Camfranglais
items.summary: Researchers released CamSpokenNLI, a pilot spoken natural language inference dataset of 228 items in Cameroon Pidgin English and Camfranglais, labeled by a single author.

items.title: Small Open-Weight Language Models for Crowd Decision-Making: Capabilities and Limits of Output-Level Fusion and Linguistic Aggregation
items.summary: A study tests whether repeated queries to small open-weight LLMs, aggregated via linguistic methods, settle crowd decisions on 474 TripAdvisor restaurant reviews, finding limits.
items.why: Running small open-weight models on in-house infrastructure keeps data and checkpoints under institutional control, though repeated outputs may not yield stable decisions.

items.title: What Do Multilingual Self-Supervised Speech Encoders Know About Sentence Meaning?
items.summary: Researchers probe sentence-level semantics in 76-language self-supervised speech encoders using linear maps to text embeddings, finding meaning is uneven across languages and resource tiers.

items.title: See Every Block Once: Variance-Reduced Post-Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: Researchers propose a variance-reduced blockwise ELBO estimation scheme for policy-gradient post-training of masked diffusion language models, sampling blocks to cover each once.
items.why: Better gradient estimates for diffusion LLM alignment could make preference post-training of non-autoregressive models more efficient.

items.title: RAG-FGO: Dynamic Optimization of Query-Rewriting Agents for Generative RAG
items.summary: Researchers present RAG-FGO, a method that dynamically optimizes query-rewriting agents for generative RAG, jointly tuning prompt templates and decoding parameters.
items.why: Query rewriting strongly affects RAG quality, and joint optimization of rewriting prompts and decoding settings could improve retrieval pipelines in production.

items.title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix
items.summary: A study of 2,000 ACL, EMNLP, COLM, and ICLR papers finds latest GPT and Claude models draw about 50% or more of review weaknesses from appendices.
items.why: Teams using LLM reviewers or evaluators should know these models may weigh appendix content heavily, which can skew assessments of submitted work.

items.title: PaperCritic: Training AI Reviewers to Assess the Soundness of Papers
items.summary: Researchers present PaperCritic, a method for training AI reviewers to assess paper soundness, optimizing precision and recall of review points on the objective criterion.

items.title: BLiMP-RO: A Benchmark of Linguistic Minimal Pairs for Romanian
items.summary: Researchers released BLiMP-RO, a Romanian minimal-pair benchmark of 493 linguist-built pairs across 50 grammatical phenomena, plus 5,942 semi-automatically generated validated pairs.

items.title: In the Eye of the Beholder: Human Label Variation in Textual and Visual Entailment
items.summary: Researchers introduce VariNLI-VE, a dataset studying how human label variation changes when textual premises are replaced by images in entailment tasks.
items.why: It shows human disagreement in multimodal labeling differs from text-only NLI, relevant for building and evaluating vision-language training data.

items.title: Toward Universal Translatability: On the Statistical Ontology of Generative AI
items.summary: A paper argues that translation serves as both origin and normative goal for generative AI, critiquing the ideal of models as universal translators across representation spaces.
items.why: It is a philosophical critique of 'world model' framing, offering limited concrete guidance for engineering teams.

items.title: FEND: Far-End Detection in Outbound Voice AI Calls
items.summary: FEND is a method for detecting the far end of outbound Voice AI calls, distinguishing live humans, voicemail, IVR systems, and other AI systems.
items.why: Standard answering machine detection only yields human-or-machine, which is insufficient for voice agents deciding whether to leave messages or navigate menus.

items.title: Agent-as-a-Judge
items.summary: Agent-as-a-Judge proposes evaluation where the judge gathers evidence beyond the supplied material, extending the LLM-as-a-Judge paradigm.
items.why: Evaluation pipelines for deployed models may need agentic judges that verify evidence rather than relying only on fixed context.

items.title: VEPO: Mitigating Multilingual Hallucinations in LVLMs via Visual Evidence-guided Preference Optimization
items.summary: VEPO is a preference-optimization method that reduces object hallucinations in multilingual vision-language models using visual evidence guidance.
items.why: It targets hallucinations in low-resource languages without costly multilingual annotation or external reward models, which matters for multilingual deployments.

items.title: Contagious Fingerprints: When LLMs Inherit Another Model's Identity
items.summary: The paper shows that a model continuing another model's conversation inherits its text fingerprint, so API relays can silently substitute cheaper models after handoff.
items.why: This undermines audits of API providers, since customers paying for one model may receive a cheaper substitute mid-conversation.

items.title: Folding Language Models into Themselves
items.summary: Concertina builds a compact student model directly from teacher weights by folding groups of adjacent layers into a shared, looped block with low-rank corrections.
items.why: It could reduce the data needed for distillation by reusing teacher weights, relevant for teams compressing models.

items.title: A Multi-Layered AI Pipeline for BPMN Generation from Natural Language
items.summary: A multi-layered pipeline combining transformers, LLMs, and ontology population generates BPMN process diagrams from natural language descriptions.
items.why: It offers an approach to automating business process modeling from text, though the summary gives few performance details.

items.title: NER-D: A cross-domain benchmark for German NER
items.summary: NER-D is a cross-domain benchmark of 13 German NER datasets across nine domains, evaluating proprietary and small open-source models.
items.why: It shows a proprietary model outperforming smaller open models without optimization, and tests in-context learning and LoRA gains for German NER.

items.title: MamaReason: Unfinished Reasoning and Answer Recovery in Clinical Language Models
items.summary: MamaReason studies clinical language models that often return a diagnosis already stated in unfinished reasoning, and shows recovery of answers from those commitments.
items.why: Answer continuation repeating stated diagnoses is a safety and reliability concern for clinical LLM deployments.

items.title: GT-FENG: General Theory of Factual Evaluation and Normative Grounding in Language Models *Author(s)
items.summary: GT-FENG is a framework that checks language model answers against jurisdiction- and date-dependent rules to unify contextual correctness and rule-based error attribution.
items.why: Context-dependent correctness in law and policy domains is a practical evaluation problem for teams deploying LLMs in regulated settings.

items.title: Learning Word-Level Explanations of Text Reuse in Latin Literature with Little Annotation
items.summary: The paper proposes labeling word-level operations, such as copy or substitution, in Latin text reuse pairs using only a limited amount of annotation.
items.why: It is a niche digital humanities method, with limited direct relevance to most engineering teams.

items.title: "Who is Hiring?" postings stuck near 12-year lows as AI reaches half of all jobs
items.summary: A Hacker News trends page reports 'Who is Hiring?' postings near 12-year lows, while AI reaches half of all jobs.
items.why: The description gives only a headline-level claim and no methodology, so limited context is available for engineers to act on.

items.title: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
items.summary: Apple announced the Apple Health AI Usage Study with OpenEvidence to better understand how people use conversational AI health tools and how useful their answers are.
items.why: Shows how major platforms are measuring real-world usefulness of medical AI assistants, a factor for teams building health-related AI products.

items.title: AI Day Seoul Brings Together Korea’s Industry Leaders, Startups and Developer Communities
items.summary: AI Day Seoul at COEX drew over 2,000 attendees to discuss physical AI and AI agents, with NVIDIA's Deepu Talla saying Korea is punching above its weight.
items.why: Signals growing regional momentum in physical AI and robotics ecosystems, though the text offers little concrete technical detail.

items.title: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi lands $24M seed round as it eyes global AI sensor market
items.summary: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi raised a $24M seed round and says it has design wins for its AI-enabled sensor technology, including with General Atomics.
items.why: Design wins with a defense contractor suggest commercial traction for AI-enabled sensor hardware, a niche relevant to edge and embedded teams.

items.title: A step toward defining the Standard Model on a lattice
items.summary: OpenAI describes a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model, with GPT-6 Astra helping develop the idea into a detailed proof.
items.why: It shows AI being used for advanced mathematical physics proofs, though the source gives little detail on the result's validity or broader impact.

items.title: Our new blog for science
items.summary: OpenAI launched a science blog to share research findings, practical methods, and firsthand accounts from researchers using AI for scientific discovery.
